title: Gandalf: Learning Label-label Correlations in Extreme Multi-label Classification via Label Features

problem.claim: Extreme multi-label text classification assigns each input a subset of relevant labels from millions of choices; this work focuses on settings with short-text inputs and label features.

contributions.claim: Gandalf uses a label co-occurrence graph and label features to supplement the training distribution with additional training instances.
It constructs training instances from label features and generates soft-label targets through the label graph to capture label-label correlations.
The authors describe Gandalf as plug-and-play across methods without additional computational overhead.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe Gandalf as a novel approach using a label co-occurrence graph and label features for short-text XMC.

author_reported_evidence.claim: With fewer than half as many training instances, the generated-data models are reported to surpass original-data training, especially on tail-label PSP@k.
Adding the generated examples to original data gives a reported mean relative gain of 5% for six algorithms on four benchmarks, whose label counts reach 1.3 million.
The authors report plug-and-play use across methods without additional computational overhead.

narrative_sequence.summary: Frames XMC over millions of labels and short-text instances and label features.
Lists short-text XMC applications such as query-to-ad-phrase matching, product recommendation, and related-search prediction.
Uses label features to construct training instances and a co-occurrence graph to generate soft-label targets.
Reports gains for models trained on generated instances and for combinations with original data, including tail-label PSP@k results.
Describes the approach as plug-and-play across methods without additional computational overhead.

source_observation.claim: Label features are converted into additional training instances, with a label graph supplying soft-label targets.

interpretation.claim: In this short-text XMC setting, structured label information can supply additional training examples.

application.claim: For short-text multi-label tasks with usable label features and co-occurrence structure, consider testing label-derived training instances as supplementary supervision.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish transfer beyond XMC or settings with usable label features and label co-occurrence structure.

unknowns: The abstract does not name the benchmark datasets or evaluation protocol.
It does not report absolute metric values, variance, or statistical significance.
It does not define the computational-overhead comparison.
